key_concepts: Food enters the body through the mouth and is mechanically broken down by teeth.
The esophagus is a muscular tube that connects the mouth to the stomach.
The stomach is a muscular sac that churns food and mixes it with digestive juices.
The small intestine is a long, winding tube where most nutrient absorption happens.
The large intestine absorbs water and salts from undigested material and forms feces.
Waste products leave the body through the rectum and anus.
Digestion includes ingestion, propulsion, digestion, absorption, and defecation.
Chewing food thoroughly helps prevent stomach discomfort and supports digestion.
Accessory organs such as the liver and pancreas produce substances that aid digestion.
Drinking enough water helps dissolve nutrients and supports absorption.
